'''''Oxalis brasiliensis''''', also known by its common name '''Brazilian woodsorrel''' is a [[species]] from the [[Section (botany)|section]] ''[[Oxalis sect. Ionoxalis|Ionoxalis]]''.<ref name="inaturalist-Oxalis brasiliensis">{{cite web |title=Oxalis brasiliensis |url=https://www.inaturalist.org/taxa/380916-Oxalis-brasiliensis |website=iNaturalist |access-date=2021-02-14 |language=en}}</ref> It was first described by [[Dámaso Antonio Larrañaga]].<ref>{{Citation|last=Registry-Migration.Gbif.Org|title=GBIF Backbone Taxonomy|date=2019|url=https://www.gbif.org/dataset/d7dddbf4-2cf0-4f39-9b2a-bb099caae36c|publisher=GBIF Secretariat|language=en|doi=10.15468/39omei|access-date=2021-02-14}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite book|last=Larrañaga|first=Dámaso Antonio|authorlink=Dámaso Antonio Larrañaga|url=https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/item/202449|title=Escritos de don Dámaso Antonio Larrañaga|last2=Uruguay|first2=Instituto Histórico y Geográfico del|date=1922|publisher=Impr. Nacional|edition=Nacional|volume=1|location=Montevideo}}</ref>

==Description==
'''''Oxalis brasiliensis''''' is a herbaceous, perennial plant with a very long but simple root and very small stems.<ref name=":0" /> It has yellow<ref name=":0" /> or brilliant crimson-purple<ref>{{Cite book|last=Weathers|first=John|url=https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/item/48034|title=The bulb book; or, Bulbous and tuberous plants for the open air, stove, and greenhouse, containing particulars as to descriptions, culture, propagation, etc. ...|date=1911|publisher=J. Murray|location=London}}</ref> flowers.
